subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should durable `/exec` session overrides continue to take precedence over changed global `tools.exec` config, or should OpenClaw add a supported way to clear or demote those overrides when operators change exec policy?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally persist `/exec` as session state, but the report raises a real operator security expectation; automation should not pick the security precedence contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add explicit reset or doctor repair
options.body: Preserve the documented session override contract while adding an operator-visible way to clear stale exec overrides after policy changes.

options.title: Change precedence on resume
options.body: Make global or agent config win over stored session exec fields after restart, with migration/docs/tests for users relying on durable session defaults.

options.title: Keep current contract
options.body: Leave durable `/exec` precedence as-is and document that hard enforcement requires tool policy deny or session reset.

recommendation.title: Add explicit reset or doctor repair
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented session override contract while adding an operator-visible way to clear stale exec overrides after policy changes.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the `/exec` session override behavior and authored several later exec directive/docs/test changes.
